newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's main car plant sidesteps French strike.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's main car plant sidesteps French strike.

text.p: Portugal's biggest vehicle plant, the Ford -Volkswagen AutoEuropa joint venture, has chartered planes to fly in components and avoid disruptions during a French truck drivers' strike, officials said on Friday.
"The materials and logistics department have taken special steps including chartering several airplanes to fly our material needs to us," managing director Ralph Rosignolo said.
The parts include engines, transmissions and air conditioning components used to manufacture passenger vans.
Rosignolo said that AutoEuropa had enough supplies to guarantee normal production until the middle of next week, barring unexpected developments.
Officials at AutoEuropa, the biggest foreign investment in Portugal, could not estimate the additional costs involved or say who would pay for the special flights.
Exports from AutoEuropa, 30 miles (50 km) south of Lisbon, were not affected as most finished vehicles were transported by train and boat, spokeswoman Carmo Jardim told Reuters.
AutoEuropa expects to boost its output of vehicles by some 20 percent to 121,000 vehicles in 1996, officials have said.
The French truck drivers' strike has paralysed Portugal's road transport fleet which exports and imports vital produce, Portuguese business leaders said on Friday.
The French drivers were on strike for a fifth day, blocking roads and petrol depots around the country in a conflict showing increasing signs of squeezing the economy.
The truckers are demanding wage rises, shorter working hours and retirement at 55 instead of 60.
